title: Flat descent of catenarity and equidimensionality
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a flat local map of Noetherian local commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; local means that the inverse image of the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Assume that $B$ is catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring] and $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is equidimensional, meaning that all its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] have the same Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak pB)$ is equidimensional, and $A$ is catenary and $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is equidimensional. Here $\mathfrak pB$ is the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: Write $a=\dim A$ and $d=\dim B$, using ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Both are finite nonnegative integers by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], the components of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ are $V(\mathfrak r)$ for minimal primes $\mathfrak r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring], their dimensions are $\dim(B/\mathfrak r)$. The common value is $d$: every prime chain can be extended downwards to a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], while a chain in any $B/\mathfrak r$ is a chain in $B$. Thus $\dim(B/\mathfrak r)=d$ for every minimal $\mathfrak r$.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, the equidimensionality assumption, expanded into minimal-prime quotient dimensions

proof.text:
For any prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$ using [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. By catenarity as defined in [def-exc-excellent-ring], every saturated chain from $\mathfrak r$ to $\mathfrak m_B$ has length $d$, and every saturated chain from $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak m_B$ has length $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)$. Indeed all such chain lengths agree in each interval, and their supremum is the quotient dimension, since chains extend to both endpoints. Concatenating saturated chains through $\mathfrak q$ shows that every saturated chain from any minimal $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak q$ has length $d-\dim(B/\mathfrak q)$. Taking the supremum over these chains gives
$$\dim B_{\mathfrak q}=d-\dim(B/\mathfrak q)$$
by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. Existence of finite saturated refinements follows by inserting primes until the finite bound $d$ is reached. This is just addition of lengths of prime chains, with no dimension formula assumed for $A$.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, the equality dim(B_q) = dim(B) - dim(B/q), with its chain-length justification

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. Since the map is local, $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] supplies a prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $\mathfrak pB$. Set $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak q\cap A\supseteq\mathfrak p$. Going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] gives $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. Then $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak q'$, so minimality forces $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak p$. The prime $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak pB$ in $B/\mathfrak pB$ is minimal, hence has height zero. Apply the height form of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to $A\to B$ at $\mathfrak q$ to obtain $\dim B_{\mathfrak q}=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$. Together with step 2, this gives
$$\dim(B/\mathfrak q)=d-\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$$
for every prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $\mathfrak pB$. Both rings are Noetherian as required by the height formula, and flatness is a hypothesis of the item.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, going down and the localized flat dimension equality

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] applied to $B/\mathfrak pB$, and prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], its spectrum has components corresponding exactly to primes $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $\mathfrak pB$. Their dimensions are $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)$, by the quotient homeomorphism and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]. Step 3 makes all these dimensions equal to $d-\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$, proving the first assertion. Moreover
$$\dim(B/\mathfrak pB)=d-\dim A_{\mathfrak p}:$$
every chain of primes containing $\mathfrak pB$ extends down to a minimal one by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], and conversely every chain in $B/\mathfrak q$ is such a chain. The quotient is nonzero since $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, equidimensionality and dimension of Spec(B/pB)

proof.text:
The induced map $A/\mathfrak p\to B/\mathfrak pB$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat], taking $M=B$, and is local since the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak pB$ is $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak p$. The quotient rings are Noetherian: an ideal of a quotient is generated by the images of finitely many generators of its inverse-image ideal. Let $f=\dim(B/\mathfrak m_AB)$; this is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] at the maximal ideals, first to the quotient map just described and then to $A\to B$. A local ring is its own localization at its maximal ideal, since all denominators are units; height there is therefore its dimension. We obtain
$$\dim(B/\mathfrak pB)=\dim(A/\mathfrak p)+f,\qquad d=a+f.$$
The two closed fibres are the same quotient $B/\mathfrak m_AB$. Substitution into step 4 and cancellation of finite integers gives, for every prime $\mathfrak p$,
$$\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=a-\dim(A/\mathfrak p).\tag{*}$$

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, the two further flat dimension equalities and their cancellation

proof.text: If $\mathfrak p$ is a minimal prime of $A$, then $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]: there is only one prime below $\mathfrak p$. Formula $(*)$ therefore gives $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=a$ for every minimal prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring], every irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has dimension $a$, proving equidimensionality of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, application to minimal primes of A

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak p'$ be primes of $A$ with no prime strictly between them. The ring $B/\mathfrak pB$ is catenary: by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], a prime interval in this quotient is the same interval of primes in $B$ containing $\mathfrak pB$, and any prime inserted between its endpoints still contains $\mathfrak pB$. Thus saturated chains and their lengths agree; use the definition in [def-exc-excellent-ring]. This quotient is equidimensional by step 4, and $A/\mathfrak p\to B/\mathfrak pB$ is flat, local and Noetherian by step 5. Consequently the argument of steps 1-5 applies to this pair of quotient rings (it did not use catenarity of $A$). Formula $(*)$ for its prime $\mathfrak p'/\mathfrak p$ gives
$$\dim (A/\mathfrak p)_{\mathfrak p'/\mathfrak p}=\dim(A/\mathfrak p)-\dim(A/\mathfrak p').$$
Its left side is $1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]: primes of this localization correspond to primes of $A$ between $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak p'$, namely its two endpoints. Thus $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)-\dim(A/\mathfrak p')=1$.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, reapplication to the quotient pair at an adjacent prime inclusion

proof.text: All finite prime-chain lengths in $A$ are bounded by $a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. Hence chains between fixed primes admit saturated refinements, and every saturated chain is finite. Along a saturated chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ each successive difference $\dim(A/\mathfrak p_i)-\dim(A/\mathfrak p_{i+1})$ is $1$ by step 7. Adding these equalities gives $n=\dim(A/\mathfrak p_0)-\dim(A/\mathfrak p_n)$, independent of the chain. This is precisely catenarity in [def-exc-excellent-ring], completing the second assertion.

source.place: Tag 0AW4, lemma-flat-under-catenary-equidimensional, the final dimension-function telescoping argument
